responseText: {"title":"The Face as Field","question":"How much pressure can a face absorb before it becomes something else entirely?","introduction":"Twenty-six works line these walls, each built from overlapping marks that assemble—and sometimes disassemble—a human face. The journey moves from single heads held together by a single dominant line, through faces dense with competing marks and asymmetric features, into doubled figures, crowds, and grids, and closes with works that swap the face for a group of bodies or two large letters. At every stop, the question is the same: where does a face end and a field of marks begin?","closing":"The letters and the standing figures at the end share the same mark-making language as the faces at the start. Whether that makes them portraits or replacements is a question the works leave open.","chapters":[{"title":"One Line Holds","introduction":"Three works open the exhibition with faces where a single dominant contour—blue, purple, or warm orange—does most of the structural work, while softer marks fill the space behind or within it.","stops":[{"slot":"W008","whyHere":"A single heavy blue line carves the face; soft lavender and yellow circles behind it make the jagged foreground feel precarious rather than settled.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W017","whyHere":"Purple arcs replace the blue contour; the head floats against open sky-blue with more bare ground visible, the boundary between figure and field already loosening.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use one dominant color to trace the head, but W017 leaves far more empty ground, making the face feel less anchored."},{"slot":"W004","whyHere":"A long face and narrow neck stand against purple; white loops mark features while an extra forehead oval complicates the usual facial map without overwhelming the contour.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W017's head floats freely, this narrow face is pulled downward by its long neck, trading openness for vertical tension."}]},{"title":"Marks Compete for the Same Space","introduction":"These seven works crowd the face with overlapping strokes until no single line governs the whole. Color, asymmetry, and repeated marks fight for dominance across warm, saturated grounds.","stops":[{"slot":"W026","whyHere":"A spiral vortex reads as an eye socket while slashing cyan lines scatter attention outward; the salmon field contains the collision without resolving it.","transitionFromPrevious":"The single governing contour of the previous chapter dissolves here into competing colored scribbles pressing against a warm, unbroken background."},{"slot":"W016","whyHere":"Broad orange and pink masses give the tilted face volume while fine blue loops keep its edges unsettled against bright yellow.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a warm field to contain a tangled head, but this face tilts and its features stay open rather than pressurized."},{"slot":"W001","whyHere":"Thick red, black, and yellow lines crowd a large head; differently framed eyes and rows of oval mouth-marks briefly steady an otherwise dense surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"The warm-field looseness of the previous work tightens here: the head nearly fills the square and the marks grow heavier and more insistent."},{"slot":"W003","whyHere":"Rectangular scaffolding in red and blue holds soft pink fills; orbiting purple and yellow loops vibrate against the orange field, giving the mask-like face a mechanical pressure.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a yellow-orange ground and crowded marks, but this head introduces rigid rectangular shapes that make the face feel constructed rather than drawn."},{"slot":"W006","whyHere":"Long strokes fan outward above the tilted head, carrying the face's restless energy into the surrounding yellow space beyond the skull's edge.","transitionFromPrevious":"The orbiting loops of the previous work become directional here: marks escape upward and outward rather than circling the form."},{"slot":"W007","whyHere":"A white X over one eye area reads as cancellation; the open red mouth with crude teeth holds the mood between shout and grin against a flat gray field.","transitionFromPrevious":"The bright yellow ground gives way to flat gray, isolating the figure more starkly and making the X-mark feel like a deliberate interruption rather than overflow."},{"slot":"W010","whyHere":"Three eye-like forms at different heights give the face an unsteady gaze; vertical bars across the mouth make the expression harder to settle.","transitionFromPrevious":"The single X-cancellation of the previous work expands here into three competing eye forms, multiplying the points of uncertainty across the face."}]},{"title":"The Face Under Maximum Pressure","introduction":"Seven works push mark-making to its densest point. Spiral eyes, bared teeth, radiating lines, and dark grounds make the face feel like a site of accumulation rather than a stable image.","stops":[{"slot":"W011","whyHere":"A small elongated face sits within a wide spread of colored strands; the contrast between narrow head and expansive surroundings gives the portrait a different scale at each stage of looking.","transitionFromPrevious":"After the crowded, nearly full-frame faces, this work pulls back: the head shrinks inside its own hair-like field, reversing the pressure."},{"slot":"W005","whyHere":"Mismatched spiral eyes and an open toothed mouth stare outward; a small secondary circle below the chin suggests the face is still accumulating downward.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works show a face surrounded by tangled strands, but here the head reasserts its full-frame scale and the spiral eyes lock the viewer's gaze."},{"slot":"W014","whyHere":"One eye is loose and layered, the other a tight bullseye; zigzag lines across the forehead and a gaping toothed mouth push the bright yellow field forward.","transitionFromPrevious":"The spiral eyes of the previous work reappear here in a more extreme asymmetry, and the yellow ground intensifies the sense of forward pressure."},{"slot":"W018","whyHere":"A pink-lavender spiral crown pulls the eye upward while bared teeth anchor below; a teal stripe splits the face into halves that don't mirror each other.","transitionFromPrevious":"The bullseye eye of the previous work becomes a full spiral crown here, and the face splits vertically rather than varying eye by eye."},{"slot":"W012","whyHere":"Radiating hair-like strokes push outward in every direction; warm yellows and reds inside read as feverish against the cool blue ground.","transitionFromPrevious":"The radiating lines that escaped upward in earlier works now push in every direction simultaneously, giving the head a sense of unraveling."},{"slot":"W019","whyHere":"Layered loops construct a head that reads as both face and skull; chain-like forms at the bottom leave the figure's mood between restraint and ornament.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use a hot yellow field and tangled reds, but this face introduces skull-like exposed teeth and chain forms that shift the register toward something more structural."},{"slot":"W009","whyHere":"Three hollow spiral sockets stare with unsettling symmetry; warm golden tones seep through dense black scribble, giving the dark mass a faint glow.","transitionFromPrevious":"The skull reading of the previous work intensifies here: the black ground and three symmetrical sockets make this the most mask-like and confrontational face in the sequence."}]},{"title":"Doubling, Crossing, and the Grid","introduction":"Five works introduce more than one face into the same image—through asymmetric halves, a white X, paired profiles, three crowded heads, and a full grid—testing whether multiplying the face clarifies or dissolves it.","stops":[{"slot":"W021","whyHere":"A white X seals one eye while the other stays open; purple scribbles spill past the face into the background, dissolving the boundary between figure and field.","transitionFromPrevious":"The three-socket symmetry of the previous work breaks here: one side of the face is marked through, giving the two halves different weight."},{"slot":"W020","whyHere":"Layered neon outlines trace a skull in profile, each color pass slightly offset so the form vibrates; a jagged crown reads as another restless loop rather than decoration.","transitionFromPrevious":"The frontal face gives way to a profile, and the single-pass outline multiplies into layered offsets that make the skull appear to shift."},{"slot":"W002","whyHere":"Two hollow-looking heads face the same direction, packed with overlapping color tangles; a coral projection from the left head reaches into the gap without bridging the two forms.","transitionFromPrevious":"The single profile of the previous work doubles here, but the two heads remain isolated despite their closeness, the gap between them held open."},{"slot":"W024","whyHere":"Three black-outlined heads crowd the frame; white scrawl layered across their faces reads as interruption, obscuring mouths and eyes and lending the group a feeling of being spoken over.","transitionFromPrevious":"The two isolated profiles become three heads pressed shoulder to shoulder, and a new layer of white marks partially erases the features that were just established."},{"slot":"W023","whyHere":"A roughly four-by-four grid boxes each face into its own cell; the purple ground pushes warmer fills forward so faces surface from noise, none fully winning attention.","transitionFromPrevious":"Three heads become sixteen, the crowd formalized into a grid where every cell competes equally and no single face can hold the eye."},{"slot":"W015","whyHere":"Dense overlapping loops form two mismatched hollow shapes; pale vertical lines drape across the surface like static, partially dissolving the face back into pattern.","transitionFromPrevious":"The grid's many cells compress back into a single face, but vertical lines now dissolve it toward pure pattern, bridging the crowd chapter and the works that follow."}]},{"title":"Beyond the Single Face","introduction":"The final four works move away from the isolated portrait: figures stand together, a group fills a field, and two large letters replace the face entirely—asking whether the subject was ever singular.","stops":[{"slot":"W022","whyHere":"Three narrow figures share an orange field; radiating side marks and a hovering oval above the central figure give the group a shared structure without merging it into one body.","transitionFromPrevious":"The dissolving single face of the previous work gives way to three distinct upright figures, restoring bodily presence but distributing it across a group."},{"slot":"W013","whyHere":"Five figures stand close together, thin lines crossing between them; loops above their heads repeat the same gesture across the group while uneven faces keep each figure distinct.","transitionFromPrevious":"Three figures become five, the crossing lines between bodies growing more insistent, togetherness and individuality held in the same tangled field."},{"slot":"W025","whyHere":"Two large letters built from layered colored strokes occupy the space where a face would be; the inner loops of the G echo the spiral eyes seen throughout the exhibition.","transitionFromPrevious":"The five standing figures give way to two letters that use the same overlapping mark language as every face in the show, asking whether the greeting replaces or simply is a face."}]}]}
